I've written the memo in full below. No data were inspected and nothing was fitted. Here are the main points:

- **The randomized town comparison is the design.** 12 of 24 towns were drawn at random, so report towns compared with control towns over Mar 2025 – Feb 2026 identify the effect of *mailing* the reports in the trial towns. That is exactly the board's question. Status: **plausibly identified**, provided the draw record checks out.
- **The analyst's before/after plan does not identify the effect.** The July 2025 drought order, seasonality and other trends all changed use in the same period. The control towns are what remove them. Adjusting for **rebate sign-up** would also be a mistake: it happened after the reports and was higher in report towns, so it is probably part of the effect.
- **The standard errors will not be tiny.** Treatment was assigned to 24 towns, not to 2.1 million reads. Inference has to be at the town level. With 12 towns per arm, the interval may be wide even with the 24 months of pre-period data used for precision.

```markdown
# Causal design: monthly home water-use reports (24-town cluster-randomized trial)

Pre-estimation memo, written 2026-11-12. No data have been inspected; no diagnostics
or effects have been computed. All facts come from the utility's description unless
labeled "assumed".

## 1. Decision and requested estimand

**Result:** analyze the trial as a **cluster-randomized experiment**. Estimate the
intention-to-treat (ITT) effect of mailing reports: compare report towns with
control towns over the 12 post-launch months. Use town-level, randomization-based
inference, with pre-period use as a precision covariate. The analyst's proposed
within-household before/after comparison does **not** identify the effect and should
not be the primary analysis. It should also not adjust for rebate sign-up (§3).

- **Requested causal question:** does mailing monthly neighbor-comparison reports to
  every household, versus mailing nothing new, reduce household water use?
  - Population: the 24 smart-meter trial towns.
  - Time zero: first mailing, March 2025.
  - Horizon: 12 months (Mar 2025 – Feb 2026).
  - Decision it informs: assumed to be whether to continue or extend the reports (Q1 in §9).
- **Requested estimand:** ITT of report mailing. This is the difference between two
  averages of mean daily water use per household over the 12 post-launch months:
  (a) if the report towns' households were mailed reports, and
  (b) if they were not, averaged over households in the 24 trial towns.
  Assumed scale: gallons/household/day, with absolute difference primary and
  percent difference secondary.
  - Notation: τ = E[Y_i(1) − Y_i(0)] over households active at time zero in the 24
    towns (household-weighted). Report the town-weighted version alongside it.
  - This is the effect of *being mailed* reports. Reading is unrecorded, so an
    effect of reading the reports is a separate target. It is not identified with
    current data.
- **Design status:** `plausibly identified`. Towns were assigned by a random draw,
  every household in report towns was mailed, and nobody could opt out.
  - Remaining gate: confirm the draw procedure and record (complete randomization of
    12 of 24, any stratification, who ran it).
  - Remaining gate: check for missing or changed meter reads by arm.
- **Supported alternative estimands:**
  - (a) Month-by-month ITT. The trajectory, including months before and after the
    July 2025 drought order, is also identified by randomization. It refines the
    original question rather than replacing it.
  - (b) Effect on rebate sign-up, as a secondary outcome.
  - (c) Effects in all 58 towns, or of reading reports. These are **not answered**
    by this trial without extra assumptions or data.
- **Recommendation-changing conditions:**
  - If the draw was not random as described (e.g., re-drawn until "balanced", or
    towns swapped afterwards), the design degrades to an observational comparison.
    It would need the DiD-type assumptions in §5, and the status becomes `conditional`.
  - If a town-specific shock coincided with one arm (rate change, main break,
    different drought enforcement), that shock threatens the comparison.
  - Estimation should wait for the randomization record and the missing-read audit;
    both are cheap.

Source: Hernán and Robins (2020), on randomized experiments, ITT and exchangeability.

## 2. Design and data inventory

| Fact | Status | Evidence/source | Implication/action |
|---|---|---|---|
| 24 of 58 towns eligible: those with smart meters | Known | Utility description | Trial population is the smart-meter towns. Generalizing to 58 towns is a separate gate |
| Random draw assigned 12 of 24 towns to reports | Known (procedure details unknown) | Utility description | Basis of identification. Obtain the draw method, seed/record, and any strata or re-draws |
| Unit of assignment = town (cluster) | Known | Utility description | Inference must be at town level: 24 assignment units, not 2.1M reads |
| Every household in report towns mailed monthly from March 2025; no opt-out | Known | Utility description | ITT = effect of mailing. Verify mailing logs, undeliverable mail and new accounts mailed |
| Reading of reports unrecorded | Known | Utility description | Receipt/reading effect not identified; do not attempt per-protocol analysis |
| Control towns received nothing new | Known | Utility description | Confirm no other conservation messaging differed by arm |
| Towns ≥10 miles apart, separate communities | Known | Utility description | Cross-town spillover plausibly small (assumed); within-town spillover is part of the town-level ITT |
| Monthly meter reads, all households, Mar 2023 – Feb 2026 (~2.1M reads) | Known | Utility description | 24 pre-months for baseline/precision; 12 post-months for outcome |
| Read dates and billing-cycle lengths vary by household | Assumed | — | Normalize to gallons/day per read period. Assign periods to calendar months by days covered |
| First March 2025 read largely predates the first report's arrival | Assumed | — | Primary window starts with the first read period beginning after the first mailing. Sensitivity: include March 2025 |
| Household size and lot size from billing records | Known; measurement date unknown | Utility description | Use only if recorded before March 2025 (precision/subgroup covariates) |
| Rebate sign-ups occurred during trial; higher in report towns | Known | Utility description | Post-treatment; plausibly a mediator. Not an adjustment variable for the total effect (§3) |
| July 2025 drought order on lawn watering in all 58 towns | Known | Utility description | Hits both arms; randomization handles it. Effect is the effect *in a drought year*. Enforcement differences by town unknown |
| Household turnover (move-ins/outs, new or closed accounts) | Unknown | — | Define the cohort at time zero. Missing post-period reads are an outcome-observation issue |
| Missing or estimated reads, meter replacements | Unknown | — | Audit by arm and month |
| Number of households per town | Unknown | — | Determines weighting and town-size heterogeneity |
| Other town-specific events in 2025 (rates, infrastructure, local campaigns) | Unknown | — | Ask operations; a shock in one arm is the main residual threat |

**Field roles and timing:**

| Field | Role | Timing |
|---|---|---|
| town_id | Assignment-unit key | — |
| household/premise/account id | Unit key | — |
| read_date, period_days | Measurement timing | — |
| use_gallons → use_per_day | Outcome Y | — |
| report_town (Z) | Assignment | Fixed at draw |
| household_size, lot_size | Precision/subgroup covariates | Must be pre-March 2025 |
| rebate_signup_date | Secondary outcome; pre-2025 sign-ups usable as a baseline covariate | — |
| account_open/close dates | Cohort and observation | — |
| read_estimated flag | Measurement quality | — |

**Additional data needed:**
- Randomization record.
- Mailing logs.
- Household counts by town.
- Account history.
- Drought-order enforcement by town.
- A log of other 2025 town-level events.

## 3. Causal structure and adjustment

Edge list (time-indexed; Z = town assignment, randomized pre-March 2025):

- **Baseline:** U_town (unobserved town traits: climate, income, housing stock) →
  Y_pre, Y_post. X_hh (household size, lot size; pre-period) → Y_pre, Y_post.
  Y_pre → Y_post.
- **Design restriction:** no arrow from U_town, X_hh or Y_pre into Z. Randomization
  defends this absent edge for all baseline variables, observed or not.
- **Treatment pathways:**
  - Z → Mailing → Reading (unobserved) → Behavior → Y_post.
  - Reading → Rebate sign-up R → fixture changes → Y_post.
  - U_town, X_hh → R.
- **Common shock:** Drought order D (July 2025) → Y_post in all towns. D is not
  caused by Z, assuming the order was regional and not influenced by trial results.
- **Possible effect modification:** reports may change how households respond to
  the drought order (Z × D). This is part of the ITT in this year, not confounding.
- **Observation:** Z?, Y?, moves/turnover → S (post-period read observed/household
  in cohort). The Z → S and Y → S edges are disputed; if present, conditioning on
  observed reads selects.
- **Interference:** Z_town_j → Y_town_k for j ≠ k is assumed absent (≥10 miles,
  separate communities). Regional news or social media could create some.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  U[U_town unobserved] --> Ypre[Y pre-period]
  U --> Ypost[Y post-period]
  X[X_hh size, lot] --> Ypre
  X --> Ypost
  Ypre --> Ypost
  Z[Report town, randomized] --> Read[Read report, unobserved]
  Read --> Ypost
  Read --> R[Rebate sign-up]
  U --> R
  X --> R
  R --> Ypost
  D[Drought order Jul 2025, all towns] --> Ypost
  Z --> S[Post read observed]
  Ypost -.-> S
```

**Proposed adjustment set:**
- Randomization makes adjustment unnecessary for identification.
- For precision, include pre-period use (town-level and/or household-level baseline
  mean, and the same calendar months of 2024) plus pre-treatment household size and
  lot size.
- Prespecify these covariates; do not select them by looking at outcome results.

**Excluded:**
- **Rebate sign-up during the trial.** It is post-treatment, more common in report
  towns, and plausibly on the causal path (reports → rebates → lower use).
  Adjusting for it removes part of the effect. Because U_town and X also cause
  sign-up, it can open a collider path and bias even the "direct" effect.
- **Mediation.** How much of the effect runs through rebates is a separate mediation
  target with additional assumptions (no unmeasured R–Y confounding). It is out of
  scope here.
- **Post-March 2025 household attributes.** Exclude any measured after time zero.

**Restrictions the graph does not encode:**
- Randomization procedure followed as described.
- Every report-town household was assigned mailing.
- Outcome measurement identical across arms (same meters, read processes).
- No differential town-level shocks other than chance.

## 4. Identification assumptions and evidence

| Assumption | Why needed | Supporting evidence | Planned challenge/sensitivity | Untestable remainder / gate |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Randomized assignment of towns (Z independent of potential outcomes) | Exchangeability of arms | Utility states a random draw | Obtain the draw record. Compare pre-period use, trends, household size, lot size and town size by arm (planned) | Balance cannot prove the draw was honest. **Gate:** confirm no re-draws or post-draw swaps |
| Consistency: "mailed monthly report" is one intervention | Defines Y(1) | Uniform mailing to all households | Mailing logs: delivery rates, report content changes over time | Report content varied by household (by design); estimand is the program as delivered |
| Positivity | Each town could be in either arm | 12/24 random draw | — | Holds by design |
| No interference between towns | Town-level potential outcomes depend only on own assignment | ≥10 miles; separate communities | Ask about regional media coverage and shared communications | Untestable from these data; residual spillover would bias toward zero |
| No differential concurrent shocks by arm | Randomization balances in expectation, but with 24 towns chance imbalance matters | Drought order applied to all 58 towns | Event log; drought enforcement by town; event-study plot by arm (planned) | A one-arm shock coincident with launch cannot be separated from the effect |
| Outcome observation: post reads observed independently of potential outcomes given arm and baseline, or recoverable | Cohort comparison | Smart meters, assumed high read completeness | Missing/estimated reads and account closures by arm and month. Bounds or sensitivity if differential | **Gate** if missingness differs by arm |
| Identical measurement across arms | Comparable Y | Same meter type assumed | Check meter replacements and read-estimation rates by arm | — |

**Under these assumptions:** the household-weighted (and town-weighted) ITT of
mailing in the 24 trial towns over Mar 2025 – Feb 2026, in a drought-order year,
is identified.

**What is not identified here:**
- The effect in the 34 non-trial towns.
- The effect of reading the reports.
- The effect in a non-drought year.

**Identification is not precision.** Identification here comes from 24 randomized
towns. 2.1M reads are repeated measures within those towns and do not add assignment
units. Household-level or read-level standard errors that ignore town clustering
would be badly overconfident. The realistic precision is set by between-town
variation, reduced by pre-period adjustment.

## 5. Candidate comparison and primary choice

| Candidate | Identified estimand | Match to requested target | Critical assumptions | Required data | Main threat | Feasibility / failure action |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **A. Cluster-randomized ITT with baseline adjustment (primary)** | Town- or household-weighted ITT over 12 months; monthly trajectory | Direct match | Randomization as described; no between-town interference; non-differential outcome observation | Reads, town assignment, pre-period use, cohort definition | Chance imbalance with 12 vs 12; differential town shock; differential missingness | Feasible now. If the randomization record is missing or compromised, fall back to B with its assumptions |
| **B. Difference-in-differences / event study, report vs control towns, single adoption date** | ATT for report towns over 12 months | Matches under randomization (ATT = ATE in expectation); stands alone only under parallel trends if randomization fails | Parallel untreated trends, no anticipation, no differential shocks | Same as A, 24 pre-months | Trend departures; few clusters | Robustness check for A. Primary only if randomization cannot be verified |
| **C. Analyst's within-household before/after (report towns, or pooled with covariates)** | Change in use from pre to post | **Not identified** as a causal effect | Would require no secular change, no seasonality change, no drought effect | Reads | July 2025 drought order, weather, prices and trends all change use at the same time | Reject as the causal analysis. Before/after without the control arm attributes the drought to the reports. Rebate adjustment adds mediator bias |

- **Primary: A.** It uses the identifying variation the trial created.
  - Implement as a town-level ANCOVA-style comparison: post-period outcome on
    assignment, adjusting for pre-period use.
  - Randomization inference over the actual assignment set: C(24,12) = 2,704,156
    equally likely assignments if completely randomized; restrict to the actual
    strata if stratified.
  - A household-level model with town-clustered inference using a small-cluster
    correction is a secondary presentation.
- **Weakest assumption:** non-differential outcome observation and absence of a
  one-arm town shock. With only 24 towns, a single unusual town can move the estimate.
- **Fallback:** B, if the randomization record cannot be verified. The status would
  then become `conditional` on parallel trends.
- **Separate, not substitutes:**
  - The rebate effect is a secondary ITT outcome.
  - A reads-based or 58-town effect needs new data (read tracking, or a rollout
    randomized among the remaining towns).

Sources: Hernán and Robins (2020) (randomized experiments, ITT, adjustment for
mediators); Lopez Bernal et al. (2017) (concurrent events threaten
single-series before/after designs); Callaway and Sant'Anna (2021) (DiD assumptions;
single-date adoption here means conventional two-period DiD is not subject to the
staggered-timing problem).

## 6. Diagnostic, falsification and sensitivity plan

All checks are **planned**; none performed.

| Check | Data needed | Assumption challenged | Limitation | Action if it fails |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Randomization record audit | Draw procedure, seed, strata, date | Random assignment | Cannot reveal undocumented re-draws | If compromised: switch primary to B; status `conditional` |
| Baseline balance by arm (24 pre-months use, same-month 2024 use, household size, lot size, households per town) | Pre-period data | Randomization (chance imbalance) | Balance never proves exchangeability; with 24 towns imbalance can occur by chance | Report; rely on baseline adjustment. Do not re-define arms |
| Pre-period "placebo" effect (fake launch in Mar 2024) | 2023–2025 reads | Arm-level divergence unrelated to reports | Low power with 24 towns; a null result is not proof | Investigate town shocks; report |
| Event-study plot of monthly arm differences, pre and post | All reads | Timing, anticipation, drought-month shifts | Descriptive; noisy monthly | Investigate; report |
| Missing/estimated reads, account closures, move-ins by arm and month | Read flags, account history | Outcome observation | Equal rates do not prove ignorable missingness | Sensitivity: fill-in under alternative assumptions; bounds; restrict to stable accounts as secondary |
| Mailing delivery audit | Mailing logs | Consistency of mailing | — | Report delivery rates; ITT unchanged |
| Town-event log, drought enforcement by town | Operations records | No differential shocks | Absence of records ≠ absence of events | Leave-one-town-out sensitivity; report |
| Leave-one-town-out estimates | Analysis data | Influence of single towns | — | Flag fragility |
| Window sensitivity (include/exclude March 2025; pre- vs post-July 2025) | Reads | Timing definition; interaction with drought | Subperiod estimates are noisier | Report all; primary stays prespecified |
| Outcome-scale sensitivity (absolute vs log/percent; winsorized extreme users, e.g. leaks) | Reads | Robustness to outliers | — | Report; primary prespecified |
| Negative-control outcome (if available, e.g. a usage component the reports cannot plausibly affect) | Unknown | Residual confounding/measurement | May not exist | Mark unavailable if none |

**What passed diagnostics cannot prove:**
- Balance and clean placebos support but do not certify randomization integrity,
  absence of interference, or ignorable missingness.
- With 24 clusters, these checks have limited power.

## 7. Implementation handoff

**Estimand and population**

- **Estimands:**
  - Primary: ITT of mailing on mean gallons/household/day over the 12 read periods
    after the first mailing. Household-weighted primary; town-weighted secondary.
  - Secondary: monthly ITT trajectory; percent effect; rebate sign-up ITT.
- **Population/cohort:** residential households (premises with continuous
  account/occupant) active in the 24 trial towns at time zero.
  - Primary: the time-zero cohort.
  - Secondary: all premises including move-ins.
  - Assumed residential only (Q4 in §9).
- **Intervention/comparator:** mailed monthly neighbor-comparison report vs no new
  communication.
- **Time:**
  - Time zero = first mailing date.
  - Baseline = Mar 2023 – Feb 2025.
  - Follow-up = Mar 2025 – Feb 2026.

**Data**

- **Data:** warehouse tables of reads, accounts, billing attributes, rebates, plus
  the town-assignment table.
- **Keys:** town_id, premise_id/account_id, read period.
- **Outcome processing:** use_per_day = gallons / days in read period. Allocate
  read periods to calendar months by day coverage.
- **Profiling:** use Polars.

**Gates (stop before estimation if unmet)**

1. Randomization record confirmed (method, strata, no re-draws). If it fails, switch
   to DiD (B) and relabel the status `conditional`.
2. Missing-read/turnover audit by arm. If materially differential, the primary
   analysis must include a missingness sensitivity or bounds.
3. Town-event log reviewed. If a one-arm shock coincides with launch, report the
   affected-town sensitivity as co-primary.

**Estimator specification**

- **Primary:**
  - Collapse to town level: each town's household-weighted mean post-period
    use/day, and its pre-period mean (plus same-calendar-months 2024 mean).
  - Estimate the difference between arms adjusting for pre-period mean, via
    regression of post on assignment + pre (ANCOVA).
  - Weight by households for the household-weighted estimand; unweighted for the
    town-weighted estimand.
- **Inference:**
  - Randomization inference over the realized assignment mechanism (2,704,156
    assignments if complete randomization of 12/24; enumerate or sample ≥10,000).
  - Test the sharp null of no effect.
  - Confidence interval by test inversion under an assumed constant additive effect
    (state this assumption).
- **Secondary:**
  - Household-month model: use_per_day on assignment × post, household fixed
    effects, calendar-month fixed effects, and baseline covariates interacted with
    post.
  - Town-clustered inference with a small-cluster correction (CR2-type variance with
    small-sample degrees of freedom, or wild cluster bootstrap). Verify the method
    against its documentation before use.
  - Never use household- or read-level standard errors.
- **Prespecification:**
  - Covariates: pre-period use, household size, lot size (pre-treatment only).
  - **Excluded:** in-trial rebate sign-up, and any post-March 2025 variable.
- **Multiplicity:** one primary outcome/estimand. The monthly trajectory, subgroups
  (lot size, household size, baseline use tercile) and rebates are labeled secondary
  or exploratory.

**Notes**

- **Power note:** precision depends on between-town variance after baseline
  adjustment. Expect wider intervals than the analyst anticipates. A minimum
  detectable effect calculation from pre-period data (no outcome peeking) is a
  reasonable first implementation step.
- **Bayesian execution:** not applicable as primary; randomization inference fits
  the design. A hierarchical town model could be a secondary presentation via
  `recommend-probabilistic-model` → `bayesian-workflow`. Priors would not change the
  identification argument.
- **Output:**
  - Primary ITT (absolute and %) with randomization-inference p-value and interval.
  - Secondary cluster-robust estimate.
  - Monthly event-study plot.
  - Balance table, missingness audit, leave-one-town-out plot, rebate ITT.
- **Claim limits:**
  - The effect of *mailing* in 24 smart-meter towns during a drought-order year.
  - Not the effect of reading, not the 58-town effect, not a normal-year effect.
  - Rebate-mediated share not estimated.

## 8. Sources

- Hernán, M. A., and J. M. Robins (2020). *Causal Inference: What If*:
  <https://miguelhernan.org/whatifbook>. Randomized experiments, ITT,
  exchangeability, mediators/post-treatment adjustment, selection.
- Lopez Bernal, J., S. Cummins, A. Gasparrini (2017). *Interrupted time series
  regression for the evaluation of public health interventions: a tutorial*:
  <https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5407170/>. Concurrent events
  threaten before/after designs.
- Callaway, B., and P. H. C. Sant'Anna (2021). *Difference-in-Differences with
  Multiple Time Periods*: <https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.09015>. DiD assumptions for
  fallback B.
- **Source gap:** primary references for randomization inference in cluster trials
  and for small-cluster variance corrections (CR2, wild cluster bootstrap) were
  **not verified** in this session. The implementation session should verify and
  cite them before use.

## 9. Open questions and next action

| # | Question | Who can answer | Effect on recommendation |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | What decision does the result inform (continue, expand to other towns)? | Board/management | Expansion to the 34 non-smart-meter towns needs transport assumptions; this trial alone does not answer it |
| 2 | How was the draw done: complete randomization of 12/24, stratified, re-drawn, any swaps? Is there a record? | Whoever ran the draw | Defines the randomization-inference set; compromise switches the primary to DiD |
| 3 | When did the first reports arrive relative to March 2025 reads? Did report content change during the year? | Program team | Sets the outcome window; consistency |
| 4 | Residential households only? Were multi-unit or commercial accounts mailed? | Billing/program team | Defines the cohort |
| 5 | When are household size and lot size recorded or updated? | Billing team | Covariate eligibility |
| 6 | Did drought-order enforcement or other conservation communications differ by town in 2025? Any rate changes, main breaks or meter swaps? | Operations | Differential shocks threaten A |
| 7 | How common are missing/estimated reads and account turnover, and do they differ by arm? | Analyst (data audit) | Outcome-observation gate |
| 8 | Households per town; are town sizes very unequal? | Analyst | Weighting choice and precision |
| 9 | Was the rebate program offered equally in all towns, and did reports mention it? | Program team | Interpretation of rebates as a mediator; part of the ITT either way |
| 10 | Any regional media coverage of the reports? | Communications | Possible spillover to control towns, biasing toward zero |

**Next action:**
1. Answer Q2, Q3 and Q6.
2. Run the missing-read/turnover audit (Q7) in the warehouse.
3. Revise this memo.
4. Start implementation in a fresh session using this memo as the input.
```
